mappings.note: How many were to travel by the evening bus -- a specific point located in the prose; not LO-1, which is discussing a composition rather than retrieving a detail.
Who the author of this lesson is -- knowing the composition itself, so the read-and-discuss-compositions LO; LO-8 covers recognising a writing style, and an author's name is not a style.
The interval between Panna-Satna buses -- stated detail.
Which town's train the bus connects with -- stated detail.
Which company men were aboard -- stated detail about characters.
Which Gandhian movement the lesson mentions -- recall of a point in the text; not LO-5, no social value is being weighed here, only named.
What the writer took the leafy trees to be -- stated detail; the reason behind the joke is asked separately at q116517.
What part of speech the underlined word in 'samajhdaar aadmi' is -- grammatical form, so the written language-system LO, not LO-7 which is about word meaning.
What kind of word 'utsarg' is (tatsam) -- word-origin classification, grammar.
What kind of word 'first class' is (videshi) -- word-origin classification, grammar.
Name the lesson and its author for the given passage -- identifying the composition, paired with q116495.
What feeling rose in the writer on seeing the bus -- the narrator's stated reaction, an analysis point in the essay.
Where the writer and friends had to go -- stated detail.
Why passengers did not want to travel by this bus -- inference from the narrative.
Duplicate stem of q116497 (which train the bus connects with) -- same detail-location outcome.
What 'samajhdaar' is in 'samajhdaar aadmi' -- adjective identification, grammar.
What the writer means by 'the engine really did start' -- the ironic turn of phrase, i.e. appreciating the shilp of this vyangya; LO-6 would treat an ironic aside as plain information.
Why he felt they were sitting inside the engine -- the comic figure the writer builds, so shilp appreciation rather than a stated fact.
Which Gandhian movement the passage describes -- recall of a point, same as q116499.
What the passage reveals about the bus's condition -- gathering evidence from the text.
How the bus's speed changed after eight or ten miles -- sequence of events.
The speed the bus was now doing -- stated detail.
Why the writer lost faith in the bus -- inference from the narrative, not the phrasing of it.
Why the writer thought the trees were his enemies -- the reason is stated in the text (a collision was expected), so analysis, not shilp appreciation.
Where he began to fear the bus would sink -- stated detail of place.
How the writer presents the scene on both sides of the road -- explicitly about the manner of presentation, which is the shilp LO; LO-8 would be right only if a named genre or style were the answer.
Where the bus broke down -- stated detail.
With what feeling the writer looked at the bus company's partner -- the narrator's stated attitude.
Whose courage and spirit of sacrifice was being misused -- the essay's social criticism, so the social-values LO rather than LO-6's plain detail.
What qualities a revolutionary leader should have -- a value judgement the text invites, so the social-values LO.
Meaning of 'udho ka lena na madho ko dena' -- lokokti sense, the words-and-proverbs LO; not LO-13, no grammatical form involved.
Which lokokti fits the given sense -- the same LO worked backwards from meaning to proverb.
